newsitem.title: CANADA: BioChem sees 3TC sales doubling in 1997.
newsitem.headline: BioChem sees 3TC sales doubling in 1997.

text.p: BioChem Pharma Inc president and chief executive Francesco Bellini said on Monday he expects sales of the company's anti-AIDS drug 3TC to double in 1997 to about US$600 million from a forecast US$300 million in 1996.
"It could double if things are going like they are going now," Bellini told reporters after a speech.

Bellini was referring to increasing sales for 3TC, which is marketed in the United States under the brand name Epivir. Those sales are being spurred by the use of 3TC in combination drug therapy against AIDS with other drugs such as Glaxo Wellcome Plc's AZT, also known as Retrovir.
Bellini told reporters he remains confident of his earlier forecast of 1997 per share earnings of C$1.40 to C$1.60, compared with an expected share profit of C$0.50 to C$0.60 in 1996.

In his speech, Bellini said BioChem Pharma's research budget will increase to about C$45 million in 1997 from more than C$30 million in 1996. He told reporters that the company does not plan to fund new research through a share issue or conventional issue of debt.
Rather, the company will seek a new type of financing of less than C$100 million in the next several months, he said.

Bellini said the additional financing would be the result of a "new partnership" with financial institutions in Canada and possibly outside Canada. Bellini declined to elaborate, but said the financing would not affect Glaxo's 14 percent equity holding in BioChem Pharma.
"There is no dilution at all for our shareholders. Not now, not in the future. It is something completely new," he said.
